title: Threshold of linear thresholds
statement: Let $n$ and $s$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f$ be a Boolean function on $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ with values in $\\{-1,1\\}$. The function $f$ is a threshold of $s$ linear threshold functions if there are linear threshold functions $g_1,\\ldots,g_s$, real coefficients $a_0,a_1,\\ldots,a_s$, and, at every input $x$, $f(x)$ equals the sign threshold of $a_0+\\sum_{i=1}^s a_i g_i(x)$, where each $g_i(x)$ is viewed as a sign.
